source_location: NED/Bosma section 3b-3c, lines describing HI orientation and velocity-field PA change

source_statement: Extreme-velocity channel maps show a bend beyond about 6 arcmin from the centre, instead of remaining on the optical major-axis line.
Bosma constructs a descriptive warp model by dividing the galaxy into concentric annuli, each allowed to have its own sky orientation.
At high inclination the minimum-dispersion fit is not satisfactory; increasing the inclination of the outer annuli improves resemblance to the observed HI distribution and velocity field.
Figure 7 contains radial distributions of position angle, inclination, rotation velocity, and surface densities. The NED HTML page exposes the profile as an image, not as a machine-readable table.
The tilted-ring model gives good agreement with observations but does not explain the north-south asymmetry of the HI distribution.
